parserRules: Stream each jsonl line, JSON.parse it, and skip lines that fail to parse. Deduplicate by record uuid, keeping the first occurrence; queue-operation lines have no uuid and should be ignored or deduplicated separately.

A tool call is a line with type "assistant" and a message.content[] block {type:"tool_use",id,name,input,caller}. Its result is a later line with type "user" and a block {type:"tool_result",tool_use_id,content,is_error?}. Pair by tool_use.id == tool_result.tool_use_id. The result line's sourceToolAssistantUUID and parentUuid both equal the tool_use line's uuid.

tool_result.content is either a string or an array of {type:"text",text}; handle both. Get structured data from the record-level toolUseResult. Its type depends on the tool and outcome: object on success, array for MCP tools, string on error. It is never present in subagent files.

Treat it as an error when tool_result.is_error === true, or when toolUseResult is a string starting with "Error: ", "InputValidationError" or "User rejected tool use". Read the denial reason from the record-level toolDenialKind: permission-rule, user-rejected or automode-blocked.
Use message.content[].input as the tool input. Ignore record.wireToolInputs (raw input keyed by tool_use id) unless you need what the model literally sent.
If input has the key __unparsedToolInput ({len,raw}), the call failed JSON parsing; expect an InputValidationError result.

update_plan state, per main session: an {items,scope} call replaces the list with its items (content, status) as given. {advance:true} marks the in_progress item completed and the next item in_progress (first pending after the current index, else the next index). {done:[...],start:n} marks each done[i]-1 completed, then marks item n-1 in_progress (1-based indices) and leaves the rest unchanged. wrap_up does not change the list.

Optionally check the replayed update_plan state against the result text "Plan updated: step K of N is in progress." (K is 1-based, N is the list length) and "Plan shown (N steps)."; if they disagree, trust the text for the position of the in_progress step.

Current task list (TaskCreate/TaskUpdate): start from the latest attachment line {type:"attachment",attachment:{type:"task_reminder",content:[...],itemCount}}. Then apply later successful TaskCreate results (add id=toolUseResult.task.id, or parse "Task #N created", with status pending and the input's subject, description and activeForm). Then apply TaskUpdate inputs: patch status, subject, description, activeForm and owner; append addBlocks and addBlockedBy; remove the task when status is "deleted". Accept taskId, id or task_id as the key.

Include TaskUpdate calls from subagent files (same task list) when replaying, ordered by timestamp. Because subagent results have no toolUseResult, parse "Updated task #N <fields>" from the content, or assume the input was applied when is_error is not set.
An empty task_reminder (content []) means the list was cleared. It happens after every task is completed, so render it as "no tasks" rather than as an error.

Plan mode: EnterPlanMode success, or a plan_mode attachment, means plan mode is on. An ExitPlanMode result whose toolUseResult is an object means the plan was approved (plan, filePath, planWasEdited?); a string toolUseResult with is_error means rejected. The user's feedback follows "the user said:\n" in the content.
Read the ExitPlanMode plan text from input.plan or toolUseResult.plan, never from tool_result.content, which can be a <\persisted-output> stub for large outputs.

AskUserQuestion answers: toolUseResult.answers maps the full question text to a string, or to a string[] when multiSelect is true. Match each answer against questions[].options[].label; anything that matches no label is free text. toolUseResult.annotations[question].preview is optional.

Agent sync result: toolUseResult.status === "completed"; the report is toolUseResult.content (or tool_result.content[0].text). Drop the final text block that starts with "agentId: "; it is a trailer, not part of the report.

Agent async result: toolUseResult.status === "async_launched" with isAsync true. The completion is a later type "user" line with origin.kind === "task-notification" whose string content contains <\task-notification> with <task-id> (agentId), <tool-use-id> (the Agent tool_use id) and <status> (completed, failed, stopped or killed), plus <summary>, <result>, <usage>, <note> and <output-file>.
Deduplicate task notifications on tool-use-id plus status, because the same notification also appears in queue-operation lines and in queued_command attachment lines.

Linking subagent files: for <session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl, read agent-<id>.meta.json.toolUseId; it is the Agent tool_use id in <session>.jsonl, or in subagents/agent-<parentAgentId>.jsonl when parentAgentId is present. The parent call's toolUseResult.agentId equals <id>.

Workflow subagents live in <session>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/agent-<id>.jsonl, and their meta has no toolUseId. Link them to the Workflow call whose toolUseResult.runId equals the directory name (transcriptDir points there too).

Subagent file records all have isSidechain:true, agentId equal to the file id and sessionId equal to the parent session id. The first record is a type "user" line with string content (the prompt) and parentUuid null.

Skill: after the "Launching skill: <name>" result, the next type "user" line with isMeta:true and sourceToolUseID == the Skill tool_use id holds the skill body; treat it as part of the Skill call, not as user text.
wrap_up: input {recap, ask?, actions?:[{label,message}], blocked?}. When the result record has mcpMeta._meta["claude/endTurn"] === true, the turn ended waiting on the user.

SendMessage: input.to (also copied to input.recipient) is an agentId (17 characters: 'a' plus 16 hex) or an agent name from Agent.input.name. A resumed agent's id is in toolUseResult.resumedAgentId, and its completion is a task-notification whose <tool-use-id> is the SendMessage id.
Expect TodoWrite, Task and TaskGet to be rare or absent (0 seen). If they appear, handle them defensively and do not rely on fixed shapes for them.
edgeCases: Many result keys are optional and vary by version: harness fields such as harnessNoteCount, toolStats and output_tokens_details on Agent results, planWasEdited on ExitPlanMode, annotations on AskUserQuestion, owner in task_reminder items. Check for presence before reading.
update_plan items can contain 0 or 2 in_progress steps (the second case adds "Keep only one step in_progress.") and can start with completed steps.
advance or done/start can follow a wrap_up without a new items call, and the list keeps its pending steps (seen once).
In all 6 observed done/start calls, done included the step that was in_progress, so what start does to an in_progress step not listed in done is unknown.
The result of advance on the last step was never seen.

Two AskUserQuestion result text templates exist (older "... have been answered: ..." and newer "The user answered: ... Read the answers carefully ..."), and question or answer text can contain double quotes, so parsing "Q"="A" from the text is unreliable.
AskUserQuestion questions may lack multiSelect (17 calls); treat it as false. Answers to those are strings.

ExitPlanMode rejection: content has no "Error: " prefix but toolUseResult does. One variant is only the user's raw text (2 cases), another is an AbortError (3 cases, toolDenialKind still "permission-rule").
Large tool results (9 approved ExitPlanMode calls) are wrapped as "<\persisted-output>\nOutput too large (N KB). Full output saved to: <projectDir>/<sessionId>/tool-results/<id>.txt ...".
TaskCreate was once called with a bulk {tasks:"<str>"} form and failed validation; there is no bulk create.
TaskUpdate was called 32 times with id or task_id instead of taskId and still succeeded.
Task snapshots can contain tasks that were never created in the files you parsed (55 mismatches), and statuses changed by other agents (16), so the latest snapshot beats replay.
Agent tool_results from Agent calls made inside subagent files (26) have no toolUseResult; the agentId is only in the content text "agentId: <id> ...".
Agent async outputFile is a temp path (<tmp>/claude-<uid>/<cwd-slug>/<sessionId>/tasks/<agentId>.output), not the subagent jsonl.
The same tool_use and tool_result records can be repeated in the same file (re-appended on resume, more than 50 lines later) and copied into other session files with a different sessionId and slug.
A subagent file listed by find may be gone by the time it is opened (one disappeared mid-scan); handle ENOENT.
Workflow input.run_in_background was once the string "true" instead of a boolean, which caused an InputValidationError.

Some task-notification blocks have no tool-use-id (Monitor or other background-task events with an <event> tag, or several task-ids in one notification); do not assume every notification maps to a tool call.
Some subagent_type values are user-defined agent names, and Agent.input.subagent_type can be missing (2 calls).

parserRules: Read line by line and JSON.parse each line. Keep a partial trailing line (no newline yet) in a buffer and retry it on the next read. No corrupt lines were seen, but a tail reader can still catch a line mid-write.
Use file order as the authoritative event order. Never sort by timestamp. Use the max timestamp seen only as 'last activity'.

Dedupe every record that has a uuid on uuid, keeping the first copy. Duplicate runs appear after resume, relocate or worktree switches in main files, with the same timestamp and a shorter toolUseResult in the second copy. Records without a uuid (custom-title, last-prompt, agent-name, mode, atis-latch, pr-link, bridge-session, worktree-state, relocated, cost-state, file-history-snapshot, queue-operation) are state updates: keep the latest per type.

Group assistant lines by message.id. Do not assume the lines of one message are adjacent, because tool_result user records interleave between its tool_use blocks. Iterate every element of message.content, since rare lines hold 2 to 9 blocks.

Order blocks inside a message by apiBlockIndex when it is an int (0..n-1). When it is absent (pre-2.1.255 or <synthetic>), use line order. A secondary dedupe key of (message.id, apiBlockIndex) is only valid when apiBlockIndex is an int.

Treat a message as complete when a line with a different message.id arrives, or when a non-tool_result user record or a system record arrives. Do not wait for stop_reason: in subagent files it is null on every line of most messages.

When stop_reason is non-null it may be on every line or only on the last one. Values: tool_use, end_turn, stop_sequence (only on model '<synthetic>'), refusal (check message.stop_details.category), null.
Take usage from the last line of a message.id group, or the max output_tokens. It can grow across lines in subagent files.

Pair a tool_result to its tool_use by tool_use_id. The user record's sourceToolAssistantUUID and parentUuid equal the uuid of the assistant line holding that tool_use. Each tool_result user record holds exactly one tool_result block.
tool_result.content is a string or an array of {type:'text'|'image'|'tool_reference'|'document'}. For text classification, join the text items. Skip base64 image data.

is_error === true means not-OK. Absent means the tool did not flag it (most non-Bash tools omit it on success). Also treat content starting with 'Error: result (' plus 'exceeds maximum allowed tokens' as truncated or saved output, not as success.

Classify is_error:true results by text, after stripping a leading '<\tool_use_error>'. DENIED_USER: starts with "The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use" (with feedback if it contains 'the user said:'). DENIED_POLICY: starts with 'Permission to use ', 'Permission for this action was denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier', 'Permission for this command was denied by a built-in Claude Code safety check', a PreToolUse hook error ('PreToolUse:' + '<Tool> hook error: ['), 'Blocked:', or 'This session is isolated in the worktree' / 'This agent is isolated in the worktree'. DENIED_TRANSIENT (retryable): 'The server-side auto mode classifier gave no verdict', or contains 'is temporarily unavailable (rate-limited), so auto mode cannot determine'. INTERRUPTED: starts with '[Request interrupted by user'. Everything else is FAILED, including 'Exit code N' (TIMEOUT sub-class if 'Command timed out after' is present), 'InputValidationError', 'File does not exist', 'File content (', 'String to replace not found', 'File has not been read yet', 'Output does not match required schema' and MCP '<tool> timed out after Ns'.
Use permissionDecision.decision === 'reject' only as corroboration. It is missing on most denials, and decision:'accept' with is_error:true just means permission was granted and the tool then failed.

toolUseResult can be a dict, list or string. A string means an error ('Error: ...', or 'User rejected tool use' for a reject without feedback). In subagent files it is only present on errors, so never require it.

Mark a turn as interrupted when a user record's content (string or single text block) starts with '[Request interrupted by user' (variant '... for tool use]'), or when the record has interruptedByShutdown:true. Toolu Bash toolUseResult.interrupted was never true, so do not rely on it.

A human prompt is a type:'user' record with no tool_result block, not isMeta, not isCompactSummary, not an interrupt marker, and either origin.kind === 'human' or turnOrigin === 'human'. In older lines with no origin, exclude content starting with '<\task-notification>', '<ci-monitor-event>', '<\system-reminder>', '<\local-command-stdout>', '<\local-command-caveat>' or '<\command-message>'. '<\command-name>' and '<\bash-input>' are slash or ! commands the human started. In a subagent file the first user record is the parent's task prompt.
Count attachment records with attachment.type === 'queued_command' and commandMode === 'prompt' as mid-turn human input. commandMode 'task-notification' is a system notification.

Turn end in a main file: an assistant line with stop_reason 'end_turn', or a <synthetic> message with stop_reason 'stop_sequence' or 'refusal'. system/stop_hook_summary follows but is often flushed only when the next prompt arrives, so use it as a late signal only.

Assistant records with message.model === '<synthetic>' (usually isApiErrorMessage:true, error in rate_limit | invalid_request | server_error | authentication_failed, optional apiError 'usage_limit_reached') are client-generated errors. Count them as failed turns, not model output.
system/api_error is a retry notice (retryAttempt, maxRetries, retryInMs, error.status). It does not end the turn by itself.
On system/compact_boundary (parentUuid null, logicalParentUuid set) the chain restarts. The user record that follows with isCompactSummary:true is a summary, not a prompt.

Thinking blocks look like {type:'thinking', thinking, signature}. thinking is usually '' (about 82%). Read thinkingDurationMs and thinkingDisplay ('updates') from the same line as the thinking block. Accept but do not expect 'redacted_thinking', since none was observed.

Handle extra assistant block types: server_tool_use (name 'advisor'); advisor_tool_result (content.type 'advisor_redacted_result', or 'advisor_tool_result_error' with error_code too_many_requests | overloaded | execution_time_exceeded); fallback {from:{model}, to:{model}}.

Subagent discovery: glob <proj>/<sid>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl and <proj>/<sid>/subagents/workflows/*/agent-*.jsonl. Skip journal.jsonl, which has a different schema. isSidechain is true in all subagent records and false in all main records.

In main files, records whose sessionId differs from the file stem are copied fork or resume history. Mark them as inherited instead of counting them as new activity. Do not apply this filter to subagent files, whose sessionId is the parent's.
Detect file rewrite or truncation (size shrinks, or the inode changes) and re-read from the start. Re-appended history means the same uuids show up again later in the file.
edgeCases: Same uuid twice in one main file (6,432 records, 17 files): the second copy is a resume re-append with a new cwd, gitBranch, version and promptId, and the first copy has the longer toolUseResult.

The same uuid in two different main files (fork or resume), sometimes with sessionId rewritten to the new file's stem, and with original older timestamps that can be about 24h earlier than the surrounding lines.
Lines of one message.id interleaved with tool_result records (main 1,770 / sub 17,187 groups).
Multi-block assistant lines (24 corpus-wide, old builds, apiBlockIndex 0 or absent).
stop_reason null on every line of a completed subagent message, including its final message.
A subagent transcript ending on a StructuredOutput tool_result instead of an end_turn assistant line (3,779 of 4,922 files).
A <synthetic> error message that reuses the failed request's requestId with a different message.id (14). Its message.id is uuid-like, and apiBlockIndex is missing.
stop_reason 'refusal' on a real message, with stop_details.category, followed by system/model_refusal_fallback with retractedMessageUuids.
is_error absent on an MCP result that is really a 'result exceeds maximum allowed tokens, saved to <path>' notice.
is_error:false Bash output whose text begins with 'Error:' (the tool's own stderr), which is not a failure.

A user rejection with feedback ('...the user said:\n<text>'): the turn continues, so it is not an interrupt. A rejection without feedback ('STOP what you are doing...') is usually followed by the '[Request interrupted by user for tool use]' marker.
An interrupt marker as tool_result content with is_error:true (2), rather than as a user text block.
A stop_hook_summary written after the next prompt's queue-operation lines, with an earlier timestamp.
Metadata records without uuid or timestamp, re-appended hundreds of times per file (custom-title, last-prompt, etc.).
parentUuid null outside the session start (compact_boundary, some attachments).

An advisor_tool_result error inside assistant content (error_code too_many_requests 117 / overloaded 19 / execution_time_exceeded 10), which is a server-side tool failure on the assistant side, not a user tool_result.
Dynamic text inside generated prefixes (Reason: [<reason>], <Tool> names, model names with a '[1m]' suffix, the 'Command timed out after Ns|Nm' variant). Match on prefixes, not on whole strings.
Very large lines (base64 images, originalFile in Edit toolUseResult). Files can exceed 13 MB, so stream them rather than loading them whole.

parserRules: Enumerate main sessions as <projectsRoot>/<dir>/<uuid>.jsonl (depth 2). Subagents are <dir>/<sid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl and <dir>/<sid>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/agent-<id>.jsonl. Never treat journal.jsonl, *.meta.json, *.prefix.json or workflows/<runId>.json as transcripts.

Session identity = file stem (UUID). Track a file by (stem, inode); its path can change. When a stem disappears from one dir, look for the same basename in other project dirs on the next rescan. If found with the same inode and size >= saved offset, continue from the saved offset; otherwise re-bootstrap.

If the same stem exists in several project dirs, pick the copy that has a <stem>/ subdir, then the newest mtime, then the largest size. Older Claude Code versions left stale byte-identical or prefix copies in the old dir.

Subagent identity: agentId = file name minus 'agent-' and minus '.jsonl'; it equals record.agentId. Parent session = record.sessionId, which equals the enclosing <sid> dir name. Never use a subagent's sessionId as its own id.

Link a plain subagent to its spawn: meta.toolUseId equals the id of an 'Agent' tool_use block in the main file (depth 1) or in sibling agent-<meta.parentAgentId>.jsonl (depth >= 2). If parentAgentId is missing and spawnDepth >= 2, search sibling agent files for the toolUseId.
The .meta.json may not exist yet when the .jsonl appears (74/648 were created more than 1 s later). Retry reading it on later scans, and tolerate missing or extra keys (spawnDepth can be absent).
Never decode the project dir name back to a path (lossy, collisions exist). Take cwd only from user/assistant/attachment/system records; sidecar records have no cwd.

projectKey(cwd, latestWorktreeState): if latestWorktreeState?.originalCwd use it; else if m = /^(.*?)\/(\.claude\/worktrees|\.worktrees)\/([^\/]+)(?:\/|$)/.exec(cwd) use m[1]; else use cwd. Strip any trailing '/'. Don't realpath (most worktree dirs are deleted). Compute it from the session's first cwd for grouping. Recompute the display badge from the latest cwd.

Worktree badge: show it when the latest cwd matches the worktree regex OR the latest worktree-state record has worktreeSession != null. Label = worktreeSession.worktreeName ?? m[3]; branch = worktreeSession.worktreeBranch ?? latest gitBranch. gitBranch === 'HEAD' means detached. worktreeSession === null means the worktree was exited, so clear the badge if the cwd no longer matches.

File location ≠ current cwd: the file stays in enc(start cwd) until a 'relocated' record, then moves to enc(relocatedCwd). enc(p) = p.replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g,'-'). Use enc() only to predict or confirm where to look, not for grouping.

Main session title, in order: latest custom-title.customTitle; latest agent-name.agentName; <sid>/custom-title.json customTitle; legacy sessions-index.json entries[sessionId].summary; legacy type 'summary' record .summary; first real user prompt (type user, message.content is a string or text blocks, not isMeta, no tool_result), trimmed to about 80 chars; latest last-prompt.lastPrompt; slug; first 8 chars of the sessionId.
Subagent title, in order: meta.name; meta.description; journal 'started'.label (or .phase) for that agentId; meta.workflowPhase; meta.agentType; agentId.

Latest wins for every sidecar record (custom-title, agent-name, last-prompt, mode, atis-latch, pr-link, bridge-session, worktree-state, relocated, cost-state). They are re-appended many times (about every 32 KiB of output), so don't treat repeats as events.
Ignore lines whose sessionId differs from the file stem (fork-inherited history) when computing activity or start time. They can appear as a large byte-identical prefix of the file.

Dedupe user/assistant/attachment/system records by uuid within a file. A repeated uuid is a replay (resume): don't emit it as new activity; optionally update cwd/gitBranch/version from the newer copy.
Order records by file position. Never assume timestamps increase. lastActivity = max(record timestamp, file mtime).
Assistant messages are written one content block per line, sharing message.id and carrying apiBlockIndex. Group by message.id; stop_reason is null until the last block ('tool_use' or 'end_turn').

Tool results: pair message.content[].tool_result.tool_use_id with assistant tool_use.id (sourceToolAssistantUUID gives the assistant record uuid). Treat top-level toolUseResult as optional; it is missing on about 98% of subagent tool_result lines.

Tail reading: keep a byte offset per file. On growth, read [offset, size), split on '\n', and carry any trailing partial line over to the next read (not observed, but don't rely on that). If size < offset, re-bootstrap the file.

Bootstrap a newly discovered file: read the last 256 KiB, drop everything up to the first '\n' (unless the read starts at offset 0), and parse. If there is no record with cwd, or no custom-title/last-prompt, and the window < file size, double the window (cap at 8 MiB). Separately read the first 64 KiB for the start timestamp, first cwd and first prompt. The metadata block was always within the last 32.5 KB in 92/92 files.
Line splitter must accept lines up to at least 4 MB (observed max 2.67 MB). JSON.parse failures should be counted and skipped, never fatal.
Handle ENOENT between readdir/stat and open (files are moved live). Treat it as 'maybe relocated', not as an error.

Directory rescan: full walk every 10 s (about 40 ms warm for 5.3k files), or fs.watch on the projects root plus each project dir and <sid>/subagents (recursive), with a 30 s full-walk safety net. New project dirs appear at runtime.

Activity tiers by mtime: live < 2-5 min, poll size every 1 s; warm < 30 min, poll every 5 s; recent < 120 min, list it but re-stat only on rescan; cold, read metadata on demand from the tail or custom-title.json.

Tolerate unknown record types and unknown attachment.type values. Classify by the top-level 'type' (and 'subtype' for system) before any deep parsing; attachments are about 22% of records and can be about 0.5 MB.
edgeCases: A session file moved to another project dir while live (relocated record). The <sid>/workflows/ subdir stayed in a different project dir than <sid>/subagents/.
Older versions left stale copies: the same session stem in 2 dirs (3 cases), byte-identical or a strict prefix of the live copy.
Fork files (2/92): the first 1135-1797 lines are byte-identical copies of a sibling session with the parent's sessionId and old timestamps; own records start with a metadata block.
Replay ranges (17/92): 2-1782 re-appended lines with duplicate uuids, changed cwd/gitBranch/version/promptId, and original timestamps.
Path collision: cwds differing only in '-' vs '_' map to the same project dir (1 observed).
Paths longer than 200 chars and non-ASCII cwds are not represented in this corpus (max dir name 176 chars, 0 non-ASCII). Encoding/truncation behaviour there is unverified.
A file's first lines can all be sidecars without cwd (custom-title/mode/queue-operation first in 19/92), and a short tail window can likewise contain only sidecars plus one huge line.
Timestamps go backwards in 88/92 main files (queue-operation stamped at enqueue time; replay/fork lines are old).
gitBranch 'HEAD' (detached worktree) in 22 files; most worktree directories referenced by cwd no longer exist on disk (595/632).
worktree-state with worktreeSession:null signals the worktree was exited (8/17 files).
Nested subagents are flat in subagents/; 4 depth>=2 metas lack parentAgentId and must be linked by searching sibling files for toolUseId.
A .meta.json may appear seconds after its .jsonl, or be missing entirely (1 wf agent had no meta); spawnDepth is missing in 111 metas.
Subagent tool_result lines mostly lack top-level toolUseResult; main files always have it.
45 session dirs have no sibling .jsonl (only workflows/ or session-memory/); don't create phantom sessions from them.
Lines up to 2.67 MB (tool_result payloads, e.g. images); p99.9 is 184 KB.
No 'summary' records exist in the current format; sessions-index.json (legacy) exists in only 2 project dirs.
lastPrompt is truncated to at most 201 chars and missing from 72 last-prompt records (only leafUuid present).
customTitle changes within a session in 31/88 files; always use the latest.

Split tool names on '__': ['mcp', server, tool]. Treat server as opaque (may be a per-account UUID - never display or send it); classify by the tool suffix. A name with no third segment is malformed - render raw.

Unknown or malformed tool names (bash, bash_placeholder, BashOutput, typo'd mcp server ids) must render as-is with a generic summary; they always error with '<\tool_use_error>Error: No such tool available: '.
If input has the single key __unparsedToolInput ({raw,len}), emit '<tool> (unparsed input)'; never parse or send raw.

Ignore unknown input keys; never assume a key exists. Coerce types: booleans may be strings ('true'/'false') in Monitor.persistent, TaskOutput.block, Bash/Workflow.run_in_background; Read.offset may be a list; tabId is a string for mcp__Claude_Browser__* and an int for mcp__claude-in-chrome__*; StructuredOutput is fully free-form.
Accept key aliases: TaskUpdate taskId|id|task_id; SendMessage to|recipient and message|content; firestore aggregation structuredAggregationQuery|structured_aggregation_query.

Bash summary = description capped at 60 code points; fallback = program name (+ subcommand) after stripping leading 'cd <dir> &&' and VAR=val tokens and dropping any token containing '/' or '='. Never the raw command.
File-based tools (Read, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, codegraph file, validate_security_rules source_file, ExitPlanMode planFilePath, SendUserFile files) summarise to basename only.
URL-based tools (WebFetch, *navigate, tavily_extract urls[0], preview_start url) summarise to host only; drop scheme, path, query, fragment; localhost is a valid host.
Truncate by Unicode code point and strip control characters; inputs contain Korean and other non-ASCII text.

Never transmit these input fields off-device: Bash.command, Monitor.command, mcp__terminal__run_in_terminal.command/cwd, Write.content, Edit.old_string/new_string, *save_issue.description/patch, *save_comment.body, *save_document.content, Workflow.script/args, Agent.prompt, SendMessage.message/content, ScheduleWakeup.prompt, spawn_task/start_session.prompt/background, scheduled-tasks prompt, ExitPlanMode.plan, StructuredOutput.*, SubagentHandback.message, WebFetch.prompt, AskUserQuestion question/options text, *javascript_tool.text, browser_evaluate.function, browser_type/computer text, fill_form fields, show_widget.widget_code, validateMermaid.diagram, firestore document/fields/filters/pageToken, auth_get_users uids/emails, outlook mailboxOwnerEmail/sender, update_environment.active_user_account, PR urls, any __unparsedToolInput.raw.

Treat these as owner-only (may show locally, not in shared output): Bash.description, WebSearch/tavily query, issue keys and titles, Agent.description, Skill name and attributionSkill, collection names, worktree names, chapter titles, AskUserQuestion headers.

Hide app plumbing from the visualisation: all mcp__ccd_* (turn, session, session_mgmt, pr, view, window, host, connectors, sidebar, settings, directory), ToolSearch, ListAgents, ListMcpResourcesTool, mcp__visualize__read_me, mcp__serena__initial_instructions, mcp__firebase__firebase_get_environment, mcp__computer-use__request_access/request_full_control/release_full_control/app_release, mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp/list_connected_browsers, mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_context/preview_list.

Use lane hints from file location: StructuredOutput and SubagentHandback appear only in subagents/*.jsonl (finish events); AskUserQuestion, Workflow, TaskOutput, TaskCreate, ExitPlanMode, ScheduleWakeup appear only in main sessions.
Use top-level attributionSkill (30,769 tool_use lines) to tag calls with the active skill instead of drawing Skill as a separate activity.
edgeCases: Grep, Glob, TodoWrite, Task, LS, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit and KillShell occur 0 times in 5,327 files (CLI 2.1.x only); keep generic handlers for them anyway.
The recent80 sample is 86% subagent files and contains no TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/firestore calls, so ranking by recent files alone misrepresents usage.
Bash.description is missing on 18,364 of 169,275 calls (about 11%); 1,415 descriptions exceed 80 chars; 6,931 contain a/b path fragments.
Edit content input always has replace_all even though the model often omitted it (2,085 cases differ from wire).
Some tools have no input at all ({}): playwright browser_snapshot/close, ListAgents, EnterPlanMode, TaskList, CronList, firebase_get_environment, ccd_pr get_status (mostly), computer-use app_release.
Tools that fail 100%: firestore_run_aggregation_query 64/64, get_issue_status 6/6, all hallucinated names. ExitPlanMode errors 38/118 mean the user rejected the plan, not a crash.

The same product appears under two server prefixes (mcp__firebase__* vs mcp__plugin_firebase_firebase__*; mcp__Context7__* vs a UUID connector query-docs), so grouping by server string splits one room.
A user-defined subagent_type can look like a built-in (e.g. a custom code-reviewer); only general-purpose, Explore and Plan are treated as built-in here.
Agent.model can be opus, sonnet, haiku or fable; Agent.isolation 'worktree' appears 8 times.
StructuredOutput field values change type between runs (confidence float vs str; refuted bool vs list); never key UI logic on its fields.
tool_result.content is a list of tool_reference blocks for ToolSearch (1,531), and image blocks appear for screenshot tools (528 image+text, 149 image-only).
Giant single inputs exist: Bash.command 134 KB (heredocs), Write.content 172 KB, ExitPlanMode.plan 122 KB, StructuredOutput field 101 KB; a tail parser must not log or buffer them for display.
A tool_result can arrive whose tool_use_id was never seen in the same file (1 case with a 'Permission for this action was denied by ' prefix), so handle orphan results.

parserRules: DISCOVER: Main sessions are ~/.claude/projects/<dir>/<sessionId>.jsonl, where <dir> is a cwd with every non-[A-Za-z0-9] character replaced by '-'. Never recompute <dir> from a later cwd, because cwd changes within a session.

DISCOVER: Plain subagents are <dir>/<sessionId>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl (agentId is 'a' plus 16 hex) with agent-<agentId>.meta.json and an optional .prefix.json. Workflow agents are <dir>/<sessionId>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/agent-<id>.jsonl. Skip journal.jsonl (different schema), tool-results/ and session-memory/.
DISCOVER: Watch for new files mid-session and tolerate ENOENT, since a file can disappear between listing and opening.

DISCOVER: Link a plain subagent through meta.toolUseId. Look it up in the main file first, then in subagents/agent-<parentAgentId>.jsonl, then in every sibling agent-*.jsonl of the same session (older nested agents have no parentAgentId).
DISCOVER: Link a workflow agent through its directory name, which equals the Workflow toolUseResult.runId and is the last segment of transcriptDir. Workflow meta.json has no toolUseId.
TAIL: Read by byte offset and split on '\n'. Buffer a trailing partial line until its newline arrives. JSON.parse each line and skip blank or unparseable lines.

TAIL: When attaching to an existing file, scan it once from byte 0 to build the seen-uuid set and the replayed state (pending tools, plan, tasks, session meta) before emitting live events. Resume re-appends old records at the end of the file.

TAIL: Do not treat the first line as the session start or the prompt. Main files begin with uuid-less metadata such as queue-operation, custom-title, mode or bridge-session. Subagent files begin with a user prompt (parentUuid null), and at least one workflow file begins with an assistant record.

FRAME/DEDUPE: Deduplicate every uuid-bearing record by uuid and keep the first copy; do this across files when watching several. Re-appended copies keep the original timestamp but may differ in gitBranch, cwd, version, promptId and toolUseResult.

FRAME/DEDUPE: Treat records whose sessionId differs from the file's stem as copied fork history and replay them without live events. file-history-snapshot and file-history-delta lines have no sessionId, so exclude them from this check.

FRAME/DEDUPE: These 16 types have no uuid: queue-operation, last-prompt, pr-link, custom-title, atis-latch, mode, agent-name, bridge-session, worktree-state, relocated, frame-link, file-history-snapshot, file-history-delta, artifact-autoreact-ledger, cost-state, artifact-comment-monitor. Treat them as last-wins session metadata (customTitle, agentName, mode, prUrl, relocatedCwd, totalCostUSD) or ignore them. queue-operation lines only mirror prompts and notifications.
FRAME/DEDUPE: File order is authoritative. Timestamps are not monotonic even for new records, so never sort by timestamp or drop records by timestamp.

FRAME/DEDUPE: Group assistant lines by message.id: one content block per line, apiBlockIndex 0..n-1 when present (absent on old builds and on <synthetic>). A group can be interleaved with tool_result records and hook attachments. Take usage from the last line. stop_reason may be on every line, only the last, or none (most subagent lines are null).

CLASSIFY: For each assistant block: text is say. thinking is thinking, and its text may be the empty string with only a signature. tool_use (toolu_) is tool_start, read from message.content[].input and not wireToolInputs. server_tool_use (srvtoolu_, name advisor) pairs with advisor_tool_result in the same message at the next apiBlockIndex, never with a user record. fallback {from:{model},to:{model}} is a model-switch notice.

CLASSIFY: An assistant with message.model "<synthetic>" is a client-generated message. isApiErrorMessage:true means a terminal api_error with error (rate_limit | server_error | invalid_request | authentication_failed | null) and apiErrorStatus. isApiErrorMessage:false with the text "No response requested." is a no-op.

CLASSIFY: A user record whose content has a tool_result block is a tool result. There is exactly one tool_result per record, keyed by tool_use_id. Its sourceToolAssistantUUID and parentUuid equal the uuid of the tool_use line. Ignore tool_use_ids unknown in the session.

CLASSIFY: A real human prompt is a type user record that is not a tool_result, not isMeta, not isCompactSummary, and has origin.kind "human". For pre-2.1.187 records without origin: string content, promptSource "sdk" and permissionMode present, and the content does not start with '<' or '[Request interrupted'. For a text array, the human text is the blocks that do not start with '<\system-reminder>'. image blocks are attachments.

CLASSIFY: Human-origin records with a tag prefix are still human actions: <\bash-input> (a shell command), <ci-monitor-event> and <scheduled-task> (app-injected but origin human), <pasted_content> and <\command-message>. <\command-name>, <\local-command-caveat> and <\local-command-stdout> records without origin are slash-command echoes and output, not prompts.

CLASSIFY: An attachment {type:"queued_command",commandMode:"prompt"} without isMeta, with origin.kind "human" or no origin, is a human prompt typed mid-turn. It has no matching type:user record. Emit it as a prompt inside the current turn.

CLASSIFY: A user record with origin.kind "task-notification" or an attachment queued_command with commandMode "task-notification" is a task notification. origin.kind "peer" or "coordinator" (isMeta) is an inter-agent message. A user record with isMeta and sourceToolUseID is a Skill body. isCompactSummary is the compact summary. None of these are human prompts.

CLASSIFY: A user text block starting with "[Request interrupted by user for tool use]" or "[Request interrupted by user]" is an interrupt marker, with optional interruptedByShutdown:true. Never render it as a prompt.

CLASSIFY: System subtypes. stop_hook_summary is turn_end (main files only). api_error is a non-terminal retry: error.status, retryAttempt/maxRetries, retryInMs, source "request_retry". compact_boundary is compact: parentUuid null, logicalParentUuid, compactMetadata {trigger auto|manual, preTokens, postTokens, durationMs}. model_refusal_fallback is a refusal notice with retractedMessageUuids to hide. local_command and informational are info.

CLASSIFY: Attachments that carry state: task_reminder (full task-list snapshot), plan_mode / plan_mode_exit / plan_mode_reentry / plan_file_reference, queued_command and hook_* (hook outcomes). Everything else (total_tokens_reminder, deferred_tools_*, skill_listing, environment and similar) is context noise.
EMIT: Pair tool_end to tool_start strictly by tool_use.id == tool_result.tool_use_id. Parallel results can arrive out of order and before the message's later tool_use lines.

EMIT: tool_end status. If the next user record is the "[Request interrupted by user for tool use]" marker, the status is interrupted. If toolDenialKind is present (permission-rule | user-rejected | automode-blocked), or the content starts with a generated denial prefix ("The user doesn't want to proceed", "Permission to use", "Permission for this action was denied", "PreToolUse:", "<\\tool_use_error>Blocked:"), the status is denied. Otherwise is_error:true means failed (strip a leading <\\tool_use_error> first), and anything else is ok. An absent is_error does not prove success.

EMIT: Read structured data from toolUseResult. In main files it is an object on success, an array for MCP tools, and a string starting with "Error: " or "InputValidationError" on error. In subagent and workflow files it exists only on is_error:true, as a string. Elsewhere, parse the content text.

EMIT: An unresolved tool_use at EOF is still running. Close it as abandoned only when a later assistant line with a different message.id appears in the same file, when an interrupt marker or a new turn starts, or after an idle timeout chosen by the UI. A result never arrived after a new message.id in 219,911 pairs.

EMIT: For async tools (Agent toolUseResult.status "async_launched", Workflow status "async_launched" with taskId and runId), emit tool_end ok for the launch and keep a subagent or workflow running. Complete it from a task notification whose <tool-use-id> equals the launching tool_use id or whose <task-id> equals the agentId or taskId. <status> is completed | failed | stopped | killed. A notification without <status> but with <event> is a progress event. Deduplicate on (tool-use-id, task-id, status).

EMIT: subagent_start when the Agent or Workflow tool_use is seen, or when a new agent jsonl appears. subagent_end on a sync Agent tool_result (toolUseResult.status "completed"; drop the trailing text block that starts with "agentId: "), on a task notification, or on the subagent file's own end: a toolEndsTurn:true result (StructuredOutput or SubagentHandback), or a final assistant text with no tool_use, whose stop_reason is end_turn or null.

EMIT: Turn boundaries in main files. A turn starts at a user record that carries a new promptId (human, task-notification, peer, or a pre-2.1.187 plain prompt). turn_end comes from whichever arrives first: stop_hook_summary; a terminal synthetic isApiErrorMessage message; an interrupt marker; a wrap_up result with mcpMeta._meta["claude/endTurn"] true; or the next turn start. Do not require stop_hook_summary, because hook-free setups are unverified.

EMIT: api_error. Emit each system api_error as retrying (attempt N of maxRetries). Emit a synthetic isApiErrorMessage message as a terminal api_error and close the turn. If api_error is followed directly by stop_hook_summary, the retries were abandoned.
EMIT: compact. Emit it on compact_boundary with trigger, preTokens and postTokens. Absorb the following isCompactSummary user record as the summary, and do not start a turn from it.

EMIT: ask_user means AskUserQuestion is pending (tool_use with no result yet). Its answer is toolUseResult.answers, keyed by the full question text: a string, or a string array when multiSelect is true. A wrap_up input with ask, actions and blocked also signals that the turn is waiting on the user.

EMIT: plan mode. Turn it on from an EnterPlanMode success or a plan_mode attachment. An ExitPlanMode result with an object toolUseResult means approved. Read the plan from input.plan or toolUseResult.plan, never from the content, which can be a <\persisted-output> stub. A string result with is_error means rejected.

STATE: update_plan state is per main session and persists across turns and wrap_up until the next items call. items replaces the list. advance completes the in_progress step and starts the next step. {done,start} uses 1-based indices: complete done[i]-1, then start start-1. Reconcile with the result text "Plan updated: step K of N is in progress." or "Plan shown (N steps).", and trust the text when the two disagree.

STATE: For the task list, start from the latest task_reminder attachment snapshot (empty means cleared once all tasks are done). Then apply successful TaskCreate results (task id) and TaskUpdate patches (taskId, id or task_id; status "deleted" removes the task) from main and subagent files in file order. In subagent files, parse "Updated task #N ..." from the content.

STATE: Keep a pending-tool map keyed by tool_use id, holding the line uuid, message.id, name and file. Close entries according to the EMIT rules. A tool_use id seen again in a later copy is a duplicate, not a new call.

STATE: Session metadata. Title comes from the last custom-title, the agent name from the last agent-name, mode from the last mode, permissionMode from the latest user record, cwd and gitBranch from the latest uuid record, and the PR from the last pr-link.
edgeCases: stop_hook_summary existed only where 3 to 5 Stop hooks were configured. On a machine with no hooks it may never be written, so the turn_end fallbacks are required.
162 human prompts and 228 task-notifications reuse the current promptId instead of starting a new one. Treat that as a continuation of the same turn, not as a new turn.

Abandoned partial streams: 12 workflow tool_use blocks with stop_reason null never got a result because a new message.id began. The new message's parentUuid pointed at a uuid missing from the file in 9 of these.

Interrupt during a tool: the tool gets a user-rejected tool_result ('User rejected tool use'), then a separate '[Request interrupted by user for tool use]' text record. That record can carry interruptedByShutdown:true, and no stop_hook_summary follows.
50 of 51 human prompts typed mid-turn exist only as queued_command attachments with commandMode 'prompt', mirrored by queue-operation remove lines with reason 'absorbed_mid_turn'.

1,190 task notifications appear only in uuid-less queue-operation lines, and their tool-use-ids are not in the main file because subagents own those tasks. 2,350 notifications have an <event> tag and no <status>.
Resume re-appends hundreds of old records at the end of a main file (17/92 files, 6,432 records). A tailer that starts at EOF without a seen-uuid set would emit them as new.
2 main files are mostly another session's history (sessionId is not the file stem). 12,759 uuids appear in 2 or 3 main files.
Timestamps go backwards for 11,425 new records (streamed assistant lines, queued_command and hook attachments), as well as for every re-appended duplicate.
Synthetic messages use a uuid as message.id (not msg_), stop_reason 'stop_sequence' with stop_sequence '' (or 'refusal'), zeroed usage, and no apiBlockIndex. Some reuse the failed requestId.
13,517 of 15,729 thinking blocks have an empty thinking string (signature only).
27 advisor server_tool_use blocks never got their advisor_tool_result; close them when the message ends.
7 nested subagents have no parentAgentId in meta.json, and their Agent tool_use lives in a sibling subagent file. 20 parent Agent results have no toolUseResult.agentId.
One workflow agent file starts with an assistant record whose parentUuid is not null, rather than with the user prompt.
79 of 92 main files contain several cwd values, so the project directory cannot be derived from the current cwd.

Unresolved by the data: whether update_plan advance moves to the next index or the next pending step, and whether start without a matching done completes the old in_progress step. Trust the 'step K of N' result text.
Results can be interleaved before later tool_use lines of the same message (18,954 cases), and parallel results can come out of order (2,233 messages).
2 workflow tool_result records reference tool_use ids that appear nowhere in their file.
A model_refusal_fallback system record lists retractedMessageUuids. Those already-emitted assistant lines should be withdrawn from the UI.
The record types summary, progress and turn_duration do not exist in this corpus (all versions 2.1.181 to 2.1.299, entrypoint claude-desktop). Other entrypoints or versions may differ.
